key_insight: TRIAGE uses dialectical, outcome-specific reasoning in an LLM to turn irregular clinical time-series signals into calibrated, continuous risk scores instead of overconfident binary outputs.
clinical_relevance: This could improve early warning systems by making patient risk predictions both more trustworthy and easier for clinicians to inspect and compare across patients.
method: Trains an LLM to generate rationales for competing clinical outcomes.
Uses dialectical reasoning to reduce risk polarization and preserve graded risk.
Converts explicit reasoning into continuous risk scores for ISMTS triage.
evidence_signal: On three irregularly sampled medical time-series benchmarks, TRIAGE improved average AUPRC by 3.3%, reduced calibration error by 81% versus baselines, and scored 20% higher in LLM-as-a-judge reasoning quality.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable rationale generation and benchmarking; real-world deployment still needs careful validation across hospitals, patient groups, and clinical workflows.
paper_title: TRIAGE: Dialectical Reasoning for Explainable Risk Prediction on Irregularly Sampled Medical Time Series with LLMs
